chunks: As for the one who said that there is no offspring for Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him),

but that there is a well-known conception here who will be born: his statement is invalid, because this leads to the time being devoid of an Imam to whom one refers, and we have demonstrated the falsity of that.
Furthermore, we will demonstrate that a known son was born to him and we will mention the traditions regarding that, which will also invalidate the saying of these people.
ai.seo_question: What is the evidence that Imam al-Hasan al-Askari had a known son besides the hidden Imam?
ai.summary: Al-Tusi refutes the 'partial occultation' (Ghaybat al-Qasr) proponents who claimed Imam al-Hasan (al-Askari) had no known offspring, arguing that this view leads to the untenable conclusion of a time devoid of an Imam (Khulu' al-Zaman). He asserts the birth of a recognized son, thereby validating the continuous line of Imams, and promises to cite specific traditions to definitively disprove this sect's assertion.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: As for the saying that Abu Muhammad did not have any offspring
and that there is a hidden conceived baby, who will be born: It is invalid, because this suggests that this age is devoid of an Imam of guidance and we have demonstrated the falsity of this.
Additionally, we will demonstrate that he sired a famous son and we will mention the traditions with that respect, which will invalidate this assertion as well.
